note: The propeller is the stand-in described in design/mccauley_1a170e_jha7660.json: NACA TR 640's measured 5868-9 maps with TR 684's tip-Mach power loss below J 0.3, blade-element maps of a 60 in helix with the 5868-9 planform at 1.27 times its chord (fitted) from J 0.4. The step between them is the McCauley's Cp(J) being flatter than any 5868-9 blade angle gives: the blade-element blade needs about 27 % more Ct and Cp than the 5868-9 at cruise J while the TCDS static band holds its static Cp near the 5868-9's; with no McCauley geometry it stays until real data replaces the stand-in, and propeller_check.py grades the steps against this record. Sourced physics carried into the take-off: the engine passes Lycoming 60297-12 Fig. 3-25's full-throttle line (180 hp at 2,700 rpm; about 155 hp at 2,300 as read here, where the research-takeoff review read 150-152), the slipstream drag of the washed parts (TR 640 p. 23, TR 684 p. 10; 2.9 ft2, an estimated component build-up), the tip-Mach loss (TR 684 Fig. 18), the POH's slightly-tail-low roll (3.4 deg, an assumed angle), lift-off at the scheduled VLOF (checked within 1 kt; the two 2,550 lb rows miss it at FS 41.0, see residuals), the gear at POH Fig. 6-9 stations and rolling friction 0.02 (NACA TR 583). The 4,000 ft ground roll stays 10.6 % short; the sea-level rolls pass at -7.4 % (2,550 lb) and -9.6 % (2,200 lb) against a 10 % tolerance. Fitted elsewhere: CD0 0.0295 and induced factor 0.0631 (e 0.67; Lowry's sawtooth and glide tests give 0.72 for a C172P, for reference), bsfc 0.434 to keep the Figure 5-8 fuel flows after the engine's friction was reshaped (inside the IO-360's best-power range). Recorded segments are excluded (card: excluded_empirical_segments). POH Figure 5-8's 2,500 rpm column is consistent; an earlier transcription error made its 10,000 ft row look anomalous.
cg: Stall rows fly at POH Figure 5-3's most-rearward CG, FS 47.3; the model's lift has no tail term and its stall solver is untrimmed, so stall speed does not depend on CG here (Figure 5-3's forward-CG table differs only with flaps 10, by 1-2 KCAS); a tail-lift term (CL_de) and a trimmed-stall solver are the follow-up. The 2,550 lb take-offs fly at FS 41.0, the most forward legal CG (Section 2), which the take-off speeds assume; Figure 5-5 itself states no CG. The 2,200 lb take-off keeps the front-seat loading (about FS 40.9): its forward limit, FS 37.5, is out of the payload stations' reach with N642SP's empty CG of 40.26 and full tanks (the loader's UnreachableCg).
